title: Blockchains Beyond Bitcoin
summary: What happens when you generalize the Bitcoin idea, and what is gained and lost in the process. Ethereum and the world-computer thesis, smart contracts and how they detonate, proof-of-stake on dimensions that actually matter, stablecoins as the use case that won, rollups and modularity, and the difference between honest decentralization and theater.
learningOutcomes: Explain the world-computer thesis and why Ethereum became a world settlement layer instead.
Describe how smart contracts work, what they do well, and the failure modes that recur even when the code is correct.
Compare proof-of-work and proof-of-stake on cost-to-attack, recovery, security budget, liveness/safety, and plutocracy — without slogans.
Compare USDT, USDC, and DAI honestly on backing, censorship surface, and historical failure.
Explain rollups, data availability, and the modular thesis in plain language and identify what is real versus marketing in 2026.
Apply the Nakamoto coefficient to real chains and defend a personal line between honest decentralization and theater.
